root_cause.text: The PPPoE flow dissector in `__skb_flow_dissect()` incorrectly tried to handle Protocol Field Compression (PFC) frames, which shifts the PPP payload by one byte and leaves the parsed network header misaligned, leading to unaligned accesses on architectures like MIPS.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the PFC-specific branch in `net/core/flow_dissector.c` (`if (ppp_proto & 0x0100) { ... nhoff += PPPOE_SES_HLEN - 1; }`) and replaces it with unconditional `nhoff += PPPOE_SES_HLEN;`, while the commit message states that a compressed 1-byte protocol field “means the subsequent PPP payload is shifted by one byte, causing 4-byte misalignment for the network header and an unaligned access exception.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Simplify PPPoE dissector handling by rejecting compressed PFC protocol fields and always parsing the full session header length.
intent_record.what: In the PPPoE parsing path, the code removed the special-case handling for compressed PPP protocol fields: it no longer checks `ppp_proto & 0x0100`, no longer shifts `ppp_proto` right by 8, and no longer uses a shorter header advance for that case. Instead, it always advances `nhoff` by `PPPOE_SES_HLEN` after reading `hdr->proto`, while updating the comment to state that compressed 1-byte PFC frames are not processed and will be rejected by `ppp_proto_is_valid()`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, PPPoE sessions with protocol field compression are no longer parsed as valid compressed PPP headers. The dissector now treats all PPPoE session headers as the full-length form, and compressed PFC frames will fall through as invalid/disallowed rather than being specially decoded. This avoids misinterpreting the header layout and relies on protocol validation to reject unsupported compressed frames.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet clearly shows the PPPoE parsing logic in __skb_flow_dissect(). It explicitly handles the PFC case by checking the compressed protocol bit: `ppp_proto = ntohs(hdr->proto); if (ppp_proto & 0x0100) { ppp_proto = ppp_proto >> 8; nhoff += PPPOE_SES_HLEN - 1; } else { nhoff += PPPOE_SES_HLEN; }`. This is the vulnerable construct described in the root cause: trying to account for Protocol Field Compression shifts the payload by one byte, which is what can misalign the parsed network header and lead to unaligned accesses. However, the code also shows the fix-style handling already present in this commit: it adjusts `nhoff` by `PPPOE_SES_HLEN - 1` only when the compressed bit is set, otherwise by the normal header length, and it validates the PPPoE session header via `is_pppoe_ses_hdr_valid(hdr->hdr)` before parsing. So the buggy construct is present, but the shown code already contains the corrective handling for PFC, meaning this commit version is not the pre-fix vulnerable state.
